These results have their own totals. They do not enter the official competitive ledger or its rivalry records. This collection includes crosschecked results and 197 clearly labelled single-source league and cup records. All contribute only to these wartime totals. All eligible fixtures in the cited season lists are now included; corroboration and source discrepancies remain open.

The game carried on.

Scores put Albion first. H/A indicate the designated home/away side; a relocated ground is explained in the notes. Scores are the recorded match scores, including extra time where the source identifies it. They are not aggregate tie scores. The 1919 Victory League and 1945/46 regional league belong to the recovery periods after the wars. Totals describe only the matches included here.

Wartime football used regional competitions and changing arrangements. This archive preserves those distinctions instead of treating these fixtures as ordinary Football League matches.

The First World War and the return

Albion declined wartime league football, then joined Aston Villa, Derby County and Wolves for the Midland Victory League in spring 1919. The club’s account describes six charity games before the Football League resumed in 1919/20. All six results are included: four crosschecked and two labelled single-source records, Derby away on 12 April (0–1) and Villa home on 19 April (5–1). The complete record is three wins, one draw and two defeats, goals 12–5, matching RSSSF’s Victory League table. That aggregate agreement does not independently confirm the two single-source fixtures. A gap for 1915–18 in this ledger does not mean no informal football took place.

The club historian on football’s return ↗

The Second World War

The abandoned three-game 1939/40 national league programme has its own annulled-results appendix. The regional leagues and wartime cups that followed are recorded here separately. The complete six-match 1940 War Cup campaign and both legs of Albion’s 1944 Midland Cup final are included. All 42 games in the 1945/46 regional league are included, with 14 crosschecked and 28 single-source records; that season’s official FA Cup results remain in the competitive ledger.

1939/40: the first wartime regional season

All 28 Midland Regional League fixtures in Albion Till We Die’s season list are represented: eight retained crosschecked records and 20 single-source additions. The six crosschecked War Cup fixtures remain alongside them, making 34 wartime matches for the season. The three expunged national-league results stay in their separate historical appendix.

The regional league record agrees with RSSSF’s Midland table: 18 wins, four draws and six defeats, goals 87–51. Each of the seven opponents appears twice home and twice away by fixture designation. This aggregate agreement does not independently confirm every single-source score or date.

Two designated away games against Birmingham, on 18 November and 24 February, were played at The Hawthorns because St Andrew’s was closed over safety concerns. Northampton away on 5 June was also played at The Hawthorns. The affected rows retain their away designation and explain the ground.

Coventry away follows the source’s numeric date of 8 June 1940, but its Wednesday label conflicts with calendar Saturday; the row flags this uncertainty. Friendlies, mixed-XI games and the fog-abandoned Sheffield Wednesday fixture remain excluded.

1940/41: the regional league season

Seven league games are crosschecked here: four against Stoke, two against Forest and the trip to Reading. The other 21 regional league results, four War Cup results and two source-identified first-XI Birmingham & District League appearances are included from Albion Till We Die as single-source records, awaiting corroboration. The November Notts County and December Forest fixtures were designated away but played at The Hawthorns; their notes preserve both facts.

The four War Cup records describe a reported 5–4 aggregate win over Notts County followed by a 9–4 aggregate defeat to Mansfield. These aggregate scores come from the same single source. The two Midland Cup matches also counted in the league, so all 28 reported regional league fixtures are represented and each physical match is counted once. Their combined record matches RSSSF’s season table: 13 wins, five draws, ten defeats and goals of 83–69. That aggregate agreement does not independently verify each result. The two District League games sit outside those 28; the source says Albion fielded their first XI in a competition usually played by their A team, and that identification remains single-source.

1941/42: two league phases and a cup run

All 33 eligible fixtures reported in the season list are represented: six crosschecked records and 27 single-source additions from Albion Till We Die. Thirteen games belong to the first league competition. The second competition has 18 games, including nine War Cup qualifiers and all eight knockout ties; these shared fixtures appear once under their cup classification. Two source-identified first-XI District League appearances against Villa sit outside those league totals.

The recorded results agree with RSSSF’s phase tables: first competition W9 D1 L3, goals 62–26; second W9 D3 L6, goals 53–43; cup qualifying W4 D2 L3, goals 29–24. Agreement of totals does not independently verify each match. The reported cup run passes Stoke 9–6, Cardiff 4–3 and Everton 8–2 on aggregate before Wolves win the semi-final 7–0.

One date remains uncertain: the source lists the Walsall home game as “Mon 23 May”. Its stated date is retained, but 23 May 1942 was Saturday; the row flags the discrepancy. That match’s date and the single-source records remain open to correction.

1942/43: North league and War Cup

All 38 fixtures reported in Albion Till We Die’s season list are represented: 12 crosschecked records and 26 single-source records. Eighteen games belong to the first North league competition and 20 to the second. The ten War Cup qualifiers and four knockout ties also counted in that second league phase; each physical match appears once, under its cup classification where applicable.

Both full league records agree with RSSSF’s phase tables: first competition W6 D4 L8, goals 35–43; second W11 D2 L7, goals 49–40. The qualifying record is now supported match by match: all ten results have individual corroboration and total W6 D0 L4, goals 19–20. RSSSF records 19–22, which conflicts with those ten scores. We retain the supported 19–20 archive total and flag the external aggregate; no individual match score has changed.

A check of all 54 rows in RSSSF’s qualifying table finds 1,180 goals scored but 1,182 conceded. That internal two-goal imbalance strengthens the case for an aggregate error. The table-wide check alone cannot locate every error; the ten individual fixture checks support Albion conceding 20. RSSSF’s published reference has not been externally corrected.

The Lethbridge Herald, 4 January 1943, page 10, independently reports Albion’s 5–1 opening win over Leicester and the 0–9 return defeat. Those two records are crosschecked. Further contemporary reports confirm both Coventry defeats: 2–3 on 9 January (page 1) and 0–1 on 16 January (page 2). These reports and the Wolves pair established six scores; further contemporary evidence now corroborates the four Villa and Birmingham results too. Ground designations remain from the season list unless the cited report confirms them.

The Birmingham Daily Post of 25 January reports Albion’s 5–3 win at Villa Park. Its 1 February results give the 2–1 return win. The Montreal Gazette scan of 8 February lists Birmingham 0–1 Albion, and 15 February result excerpts from the Times of Ceylon and Times of India give Albion 2–1 Birmingham. The British Newspaper Archive links open public search excerpts; their full article scans were not inspected. Those syndicated result lists may share a wire source. Each fixture is counted once.

The reported knockout scores give Albion a 4–1 aggregate win over Coventry, followed by a 6–5 aggregate defeat to Chesterfield. These ties use single-source scores. Three away fixtures against Birmingham were played at Villa Park because of air-raid damage at St Andrew’s; the affected rows explain the ground while retaining the away designation.

1943/44: the Midland Cup season

All 39 eligible fixtures in Albion Till We Die’s season list are represented: eight retained crosschecked records and 31 single-source additions. Eighteen games belong to the first North league competition and 21 to the second. The ten War Cup qualifiers and all ten Midland Cup games also counted in the second league phase; each physical match appears once under its cup classification.

Albion failed to reach the War Cup knockout stage but won the Midland Cup. The campaign includes four qualifying games, a reported 3–2 aggregate win over Walsall and 4–2 over Stoke, then the crosschecked 6–5 final victory over Forest after extra time.

The first league phase agrees with RSSSF: W8 D3 L7, goals 42–44. War Cup qualifying also agrees: W2 D4 L4, goals 24–29. The second league phase reconciles to W5 D9 L7, goals 46–48 when the final’s documented 2–2 regulation score is used. This ledger retains the 4–3 cup score after extra time, so its match-score totals differ from that league table. Agreement of aggregate records does not independently confirm each single-source result.

Two source date issues remain visible in the rows: Birmingham at home follows 27 December 1943, with the source noting an alternative 26 December date; Villa away follows 10 April 1944, although the source calls it Saturday and the calendar says Monday. Four mixed first-/second-XI friendlies remain excluded.

1944/45: the last full wartime season

All 40 fixtures in Albion Till We Die’s season list are represented: four retained crosschecked records and 36 single-source additions. Eighteen games belong to the first North league competition and 22 to the second. Ten War Cup qualifiers, two War Cup knockout games and two Midland Cup games also counted in the second league phase; each physical match appears once under its cup classification.

All three aggregate records agree with RSSSF: first competition W9 D4 L5, goals 36–30; second W6 D7 L9, goals 39–44; War Cup qualifying W3 D4 L3, goals 20–15. These checks establish consistency of the totals, not independent confirmation of each score. The reported cup ties ended in an 8–5 aggregate defeat to Bristol City and 3–1 to Leicester. The source does not identify the Midland Cup round, so the rows leave it unspecified.

The Villa away game on 26 December stopped after 81 minutes because of fog. The source explicitly says the result was allowed to stand, so the reported 4–3 win is included with a single-source note. Interrupted games without a standing result remain excluded.

1945/46: the return towards normal football

All 42 Football League South fixtures in Albion Till We Die’s season list are represented: 14 retained crosschecked records and 28 single-source additions. This was a recovery season after the war, with regional league arrangements continuing before the national Football League resumed in 1946/47.

The results total 22 wins, eight draws and 12 defeats, goals 104–69, matching Greens on Screen’s league table. Each of the 21 opponents appears once home and once away. Agreement of season totals is a consistency check, not independent confirmation of every match. Arsenal away on 12 January was played at White Hart Lane; its row preserves the venue note.

The four official FA Cup matches against Cardiff and Derby remain in the competitive ledger. The three overseas tour fixtures in May are excluded from this regional league record.

Coverage and further checks

All eligible fixtures in the cited 1919 Victory League and 1939–46 seasonal lists are now included within this archive’s scope. “Listed fixtures included” describes coverage of those source lists, not independent confirmation of every result or a claim to include all football Albion ever played. The evidence breakdown distinguishes crosschecked and single-source records. Single-source scores are explicitly labelled and remain open to correction. Records without a usable date, score or first-team identification remain outside the table; any retained source discrepancy is stated in its row. Ordinary friendlies, reserve games, testimonials and interrupted matches without a standing result are not part of this collection.

Some fixtures served more than one wartime competition. We count a played fixture once, retaining the source’s competition description and any relevant note.

Check the record.

Crosschecked match facts are compared across Albion Till We Die, opponents’ archives and contemporary newspaper reports. Each row’s “Source” opens the recorded result. A “Check” link appears only when corroboration is available; a single-source label means that no second confirming record has yet been established. Historical club names are retained where recorded. Some corroboration uses clearly identified public newspaper search excerpts; a full scan is not claimed where it was not inspected. Original articles and photographs are not reproduced.

References include Wolves Complete History, the Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation (including Peter Kungler’s wartime compilations, acknowledged under their stated reuse permission), and the club historian. RSSSF season tables help check aggregate records; they do not establish an individual match’s date or score on their own.

This page has no live feed. Further verified historical research will be added through published updates. The main results page keeps its existing free current-season update service.
